title: Prepared curriculum materials linked to 2026 draft benchmarks

statusDefinitions.not_assessed: No benchmark-level availability check has been recorded. This does not mean materials are unavailable.
statusDefinitions.located: At least one potentially relevant resource was located; fit or accessibility may still need review.
statusDefinitions.verified: A reviewer checked the resource for benchmark fit and recorded its access and redistribution status.
statusDefinitions.none_found_in_search: A bounded search found no resource; the search scope and date must be recorded. This is not proof that none exists.

inventoryNote: Focused first pass, not a search of all possible curricula or all 1,512 draft benchmarks. Matched items below were checked against the Florida benchmark wording and the curriculum publisher's stated NGSS performance expectations/lesson descriptions. Unlisted benchmarks remain not_assessed. Fit can be partial; read each rationale before adopting a resource.

resources.title: OpenSciEd 8.6 Natural Selection & Common Ancestry
resources.format: Full open unit with teacher/student materials, 15 lessons, datasets, readings, models, assessments, and kit list
resources.benchmarkFit: Lessons 7–13 develop and assess a general natural-selection model. Publisher explicitly lists MS-LS4-4 and MS-LS4-6, which cover the conditions for selection and how selection changes trait frequencies over time. Related but not an FDOE endorsement or exact one-to-one crosswalk.
resources.accessibility: Unit examples and downloadable materials are provided as PDFs/Google Docs; accessibility of every file and interactive item was not independently audited. Hands-on materials may need to be sourced or purchased.

resources.title: OpenSciEd 6.3 Weather, Climate & Water Cycling
resources.format: Full open unit with 22 lessons, teacher/student materials, weather observations, simulations, and kit list
resources.gradeFit: Grade 6; relevant content may support the 2026 grade-8 benchmark but requires grade-appropriate adaptation
resources.benchmarkFit: Strong topic match: the unit explicitly develops weather versus climate and builds toward MS-ESS2-6 (atmospheric/oceanic circulation and regional climate) through weather investigations and longer-term climate patterns. Check lesson materials for the precise benchmark-level expected distinction.
resources.accessibility: Unit examples/downloads include PDF and Google Docs; simulations and digital data activities also occur. No independent accessibility-conformance audit was located. Hands-on materials may need sourcing.
resources.redistribution: OpenSciEd states its middle-school curriculum is CC BY 4.0; attribute and retain notices. Link to source; no files mirrored here.

resources.title: OpenSciEd 7.6 Earth's Resources & Human Impact
resources.format: Full open unit with 6–7 week sequence, climate datasets, carbon-system models, evidence evaluation, solution design, and kit list
resources.benchmarkFit: Directly addresses climate-change patterns and causes. The publisher states students analyze long-term temperature/precipitation change, gather evidence about changing greenhouse-gas concentrations and fossil-fuel combustion, model a carbon system, and evaluate response strategies. This is a strong supplement for the climate-change dimension; not a replacement for the physical Earth-system mechanisms in Unit 6.3.
resources.accessibility: PDF/Google Docs materials and some digital data/simulations; no independent accessibility audit located.
resources.redistribution: Middle-school curriculum is stated to be CC BY 4.0; attribution required. Link to source; no files mirrored here.

resources.title: OpenSciEd B.4 Natural Selection & Evolution of Populations
resources.format: Full high-school biology unit with investigations, datasets, simulations, lessons, transfer tasks, and assessments
resources.gradeFit: High school; fourth unit in OpenSciEd Biology
resources.benchmarkFit: Strong concept fit: the unit directly develops genetic variation in populations and natural selection (HS-LS4-2, HS-LS4-3, HS-LS4-4), using population data and case studies of urbanization. Relevant to understanding variation within populations, though it addresses more than the specific Florida wording.

resources.title: OpenSciEd C.1 Thermodynamics in Earth's Systems
resources.format: Full high-school chemistry unit with 13 lessons, experiments, energy/sea-level simulations, teacher/student materials, and kit list
resources.gradeFit: High school; first OpenSciEd Chemistry unit
resources.benchmarkFit: Strong: explicitly builds toward HS-ESS2-4, modeling variations in energy flowing into/out of Earth systems and resulting climate change. Uses radiation/energy models, historical data, and greenhouse-effect simulation. Unit is centered on polar ice melt and sea-level rise, so consult lessons for exact breadth.
resources.accessibility: Unit page offers PDFs/Google Docs and simulations; no independent accessibility audit of every component located. Some hands-on resources or lab materials may require local sourcing.
resources.redistribution: OpenSciEd states its high-school curriculum is CC BY-NC 4.0; noncommercial sharing/adaptation with attribution under the license. Link to source; no files mirrored here.
